The call computes the table and its derivatives once, at the
component’s own parameters. Each call of `table` inverts the
component again at the new parameters, with the held energies. Each
derivative of `table` calls table_jacobian. The steps of the finite
differences in \(\beta_{\rm c}\) are measured once, at the
component’s own parameters, and are used at every `theta`.

References

Notes Eq. (T:7.1).

Examples

```python
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> from pianistpy.df.gradient import make_inversion_table
>>> halo = pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist(), pp.Anisotropy(r_a=10.0))
>>> table, params, values = make_inversion_table(halo, pp.Settings())
>>> params
('r_a',)
>>> "k" in values, "k" in table(np.array([10.0]))
(True, False)
```

pianistpy.df.gradient.rows_jacobian(*component*, *settings*, *q=None*, *steps=None*)

Return the DF at fixed energies and its derivatives in the anisotropy.

The values are the DF \(F(Q)\) that compute_df makes, at the
relative energies q. The derivatives are those of \(F\) in the
component’s anisotropy parameters at fixed q. For the derivatives of
every array of the DF’s table (the nodes below the table, the form at
the center and the tail), call table_jacobian instead.

Parameters:

- **component** ([*Component*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Component)) – Component on an analytic profile (not a TruncatedProfile), with
constant, isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt Type I or Type II, or COM Type
I anisotropy.

- **settings** ([*Settings*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings#pianistpy.settings.Settings)) – Numerical settings, the same as those given to compute_df.

- **q** (*array-like**, **shape** (**n**,**)**, **optional*) – Relative energies \(Q\), increasing, in internal units.
Default: `None`, which means the energies that inversion_nodes
returns for component and settings.

- **steps** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*, **optional*) – Dictionary that keeps the steps of the finite differences in
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) between calls. A call reads the steps from
steps where steps holds steps for the call’s profile, anisotropy
family, anisotropy kind, settings and form of the inversion. A call
otherwise measures the steps and writes them into steps. Passing
one dictionary to a sequence of calls makes every later call use the
steps that the first call measured. Default: `None`, which means
each call measures its own steps and keeps them nowhere.

Returns:

- **q** (*ndarray, shape (n,)*) – Relative energies \(Q\), in internal units: q as given, or
the energies of inversion_nodes.

- **f** (*ndarray, shape (n,)*) – DF \(F(Q)\) at q, as compute_df makes it, in internal units.

- **jac** (*dict of ndarray*) – Derivatives of \(F\) at q, each with the shape of q, in
internal units. The key `"beta_c"` holds
\(\partial F/\partial\beta_{\rm c}\) and the key `"r_a"` holds
\(\partial F/\partial R_{\rm a}\), for the parameters that the
anisotropy family has.

- **record** (*dict*) – Description of the finite differences in \(\beta_{\rm c}\). The
record is an empty dict for an Osipkov-Merritt component, which has
no parameter \(\beta_{\rm c}\). The entry `"exponent"` is
`"central"` where the form of the inversion on one side of
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) equals the form on the other side, and
`"one-sided"` at a \(\beta_{\rm c}\)
where the form changes (such as \(\beta_{\rm c} = 0\) or a
half-integer \(\beta_{\rm c}\)). The entry `"steps"` holds the
steps, `"pilots"` the trial steps from which the steps were
derived, `"regions"` the widths in \(\beta_{\rm c}\) over which
the form does not change, and `"measured"` whether the call
measured the steps instead of reading them from steps. The entry
`"accuracy"` is the inversion’s own accuracy, the change of the
operator’s values when the number of quadrature nodes doubles. The
entry `"residual"` is the Richardson residual
\(\max|E(d) - E(d/2)|\) of the finite differences at the step
\(d\). A one-sided record also holds `"sides"`, the number of
sides (2), and `"spread"`, the largest difference between the
derivatives from the two sides. The entries `"accuracy"`,
`"residual"` and `"spread"` are relative to
\(\max|\partial F/\partial\beta_{\rm c}|\) over q, so the
relative error of an entry of \(\partial F/\partial\beta_{\rm c}\)
far below that maximum can exceed `"residual"`.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If component is on a TruncatedProfile.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the anisotropy is COM Type II, whose interior point at the
    potential \(P(R_{\rm a})\) moves with both parameters.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If a derivative of the auxiliary density is not finite at q.

Return type:

[tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[*ndarray*](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray), [*ndarray*](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray), [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [*ndarray*](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray)], [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

See also

[`inversion_nodes`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.gradient.inversion_nodes)
The energies at which compute_df evaluates the DF.

[`make_inversion_rows`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.gradient.make_inversion_rows)
The DF at fixed energies as a JAX function of the parameters.

[`table_jacobian`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.gradient.table_jacobian)
The derivatives of every array of the DF’s table.

Notes

Each derivative is \(T_b\) applied to the closed-form derivative of
the source \(g\). The derivative in \(\beta_{\rm c}\) adds the
finite differences of the operator \(T_b\) in \(b\).

A call inverts the component once for \(F\) and once per parameter.
In \(\beta_{\rm c}\), a call also inverts the component at every
point of the finite differences, at settings and at twice the
quadrature nodes of settings.

References

Notes Eq. (T:7.1).

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> from pianistpy.df.gradient import rows_jacobian
>>> halo = pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist(), pp.Anisotropy(r_a=10.0))
>>> q, f, jac, record = rows_jacobian(halo, pp.Settings())
>>> sorted(jac), jac["r_a"].shape == q.shape, record
(['r_a'], True, {})
```

pianistpy.df.gradient.table_jacobian(*component*, *settings*, *q=None*, *steps=None*)

Return the arrays of the DF’s table and their derivatives in the anisotropy.

The values are the arrays of the table that compute_df makes for the
component. The derivatives are those of each array in the component’s
anisotropy parameters, with the energies and every discrete choice of
the table held at the component’s own parameters. The discrete choices
are the placement of the energies, the form of the inversion, the
anchor of the form at the center and the nodes kept. For the DF at the
energies of the inversion alone, call rows_jacobian instead.

Parameters:

- **component** ([*Component*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Component)) – Component with constant, isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt Type I or Type
II, or COM Type I anisotropy, on an analytic profile or on a
TruncatedProfile (Method II).

- **settings** ([*Settings*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings#pianistpy.settings.Settings)) – Numerical settings, the same as those given to compute_df.

- **q** (*array-like**, **shape** (**n**,**)**, **optional*) – Relative energies \(Q\), increasing, in internal units, for a
component on an analytic profile. Default: `None`, which means
the energies that inversion_nodes returns for component and
settings. A component on a TruncatedProfile takes the energies
of its own solve and accepts only `None`.

- **steps** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)*, **optional*) – Dictionary that keeps the steps of the finite differences in
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) between calls, as in rows_jacobian.
Default: `None`, which means each call measures its own steps and
keeps them nowhere.

Returns:

- **values** (*dict of ndarray*) – Arrays of the table, in internal units. For a component on an
analytic profile, `k` holds the energies of the table,
`log_df` the base-10 logarithm of the DF at `k`, and
`log_df_slope` the slope \({\rm d}\log_{10} F/{\rm d}\ln Q\)
at `k`. Where the table has nodes below its first energy,
`k_below`, `log_df_below` and `log_df_slope_below` hold the
energy, the logarithm of the DF and the slope at those nodes. Where
the table has a closed form above its anchor,
\(F = a_{\rm anchor} (u/u_{\rm anchor})^\kappa + b + d\,u\) in
the depth \(u = 1 - Q\), `central` holds the array
\((\kappa, a_{\rm anchor}, b, d)\). Where the table has a tail
below its lowest node, `tail` holds the tail’s exponent,
amplitude and logarithmic exponent. For a component on a
TruncatedProfile, the keys are `k`, `log_df`, `edge_law`
(the power and the two coefficients of the edge law below the
floor, where the component has one) and `center` (the exponent
and the amplitude of the center’s closed form, and the next term’s
exponent and coefficient where the center’s form states them).

- **jac** (*dict of dict of ndarray*) – Derivatives `jac[name][key]` of `values[key]` in the parameter
`name` (`"beta_c"` or `"r_a"`), for every key of values
except the energies `k` and `k_below`, each with the shape of
`values[key]`. Where a Type II DF is outside its support, the
derivatives of `log_df` and `log_df_slope` are 0.

- **record** (*dict*) – Description of the finite differences in \(\beta_{\rm c}\),
with the entries of the record of rows_jacobian in absolute
values, not relative ones. For a component on an analytic profile,
`record["rows"]` describes the finite differences of the DF and
its slope at the energies of the inversion, and `record["below"]`,
where present, describes the finite differences at the nodes below
the table. For a component
on a TruncatedProfile, `record["rows"]` describes the finite
differences of the DF, and `record["grid"]` states the number of
energies, the number of energies kept, and the energy around which
the energies are placed.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the anisotropy is COM Type II, whose interior point at the
    potential \(P(R_{\rm a})\) moves with both parameters.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If component is on an analytic profile and the DF’s center lies
    on the critical branch, where the inner slope \(\gamma\) of the
    density equals \(2\beta_{\rm c}\), with a divergent center of a
    Type I model or with a closed form above the anchor.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If component is on a TruncatedProfile and the DF’s center is
    not on the regular branch \(\gamma > 2\beta_{\rm c}\), or the
    solve of component finds the center in the band of
    \(\beta_{\rm c}\) around the critical branch.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If q is given for a component on a TruncatedProfile.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If component is on a TruncatedProfile that Method II does not
    invert. Method II does not invert a profile that carries no DF of
    its own model, a profile whose model’s anisotropy is neither
    isotropic nor Osipkov-Merritt Type I, a component whose
    \(\beta_{\rm c}\) needs sources of an order above 3, or a Type
    II component whose \(R_{\rm a}\) does not lie outside the
    profile’s edge.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If a value of the DF inside the table is not finite or is 0, or
    exceeds \(10^{300}\) where no closed form covers the center.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the tail’s logarithmic exponent below the floor is not finite.

- [**UnphysicalModelError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.UnphysicalModelError) – If component is on a TruncatedProfile whose model is truncated
    but not spatially finite.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If a derivative of the auxiliary density is not finite at the
    energies, or if the DF of a component on a TruncatedProfile has a
    defective band at the top of its energies.

Return type:

[tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [*ndarray*](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray)], [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [*ndarray*](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.html#numpy.ndarray)]], [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

See also

[`make_inversion_table`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.gradient.make_inversion_table)
The arrays of the DF’s table as a JAX function of the parameters.

[`rows_jacobian`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.gradient.rows_jacobian)
The DF and its derivatives at the energies of the inversion.

[`inversion_nodes`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.gradient.inversion_nodes)
The energies at which compute_df evaluates the DF.

Notes

The derivative of each array of the table follows by the chain rule
from the derivatives of the DF at the energies of the inversion and
from the closed-form derivatives of the center’s exponent and
amplitude.

A call costs several inversions of the component, as rows_jacobian
does, and for a component on a TruncatedProfile one solve of the
component in addition.

References

Notes Eq. (T:7.1).

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> from pianistpy.df.gradient import table_jacobian
>>> halo = pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist(), pp.Anisotropy(r_a=10.0))
>>> values, jac, record = table_jacobian(halo, pp.Settings())
>>> sorted(jac)
['r_a']
>>> jac["r_a"]["log_df"].shape == values["log_df"].shape
True
```


---

# Particles

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles

Module `pianistpy.particles`

Particle sampling: the sampler, the particle result and the particle writers.

A user builds a Sampler from a model once, then calls Sampler.sample for
a Particles object and Particles.write to write the particles to a file
in one of the layouts of `PARTICLE_WRITERS`.

Every particle is drawn by inversion, with no rejection step. The radius
\(r\) of a particle solves \(M(r)/M(r_{\rm s}) = u_r\), where
\(M(r)\) is the mass enclosed within \(r\), \(r_{\rm s}\) is the
outer radius of the sampling and \(u_r\) is a uniform random number
between 0 and 1. The velocity of a particle is drawn from the model’s
distribution of velocity at the potential \(\Psi(r)\) of the particle’s
radius. The derivation is in Notes Section T:5.

class pianistpy.particles.Particles(*position*, *velocity*, *mass*, *component*, *component_names*, *unit_system*, *units*, *identity*, *parent*)

A particle realization of a model: positions, velocities, masses and
component labels.

Sampler.sample returns a Particles object. Particles.write writes the
particles to a file, and read reads a file of the native layout back
into a Particles object. Each parameter below is kept as an attribute
with the same spelling as the parameter, and the four arrays are
read-only.

Parameters:

- **position** (*array-like**, **shape** (**n**, **3**)*) – Cartesian positions of the n particles, in the unit that
`units["position"]` gives.

- **velocity** (*array-like**, **shape** (**n**, **3**)*) – Cartesian velocities of the n particles, in the unit that
`units["velocity"]` gives.

- **mass** (*array-like**, **shape** (**n**,**)*) – Masses of the n particles, in the unit that `units["mass"]` gives.
The length of mass sets the number of particles n.

- **component** (*array-like** of *[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, **shape** (**n**,**)*) – Index into component_names of the component each particle belongs
to, from 0 to the number of names minus one.

- **component_names** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)* of *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Names of the model’s components.

- **unit_system** (*{"internal"**, **"model"**, **"physical"}*) – Unit system of position, velocity and mass. Sampler.sample
writes the particles in the unit system of the model that the
sampler draws from (Model.to).

- **units** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)* of **str to str*) – Units of the positions, the velocities and the masses as text, under
the keys `"position"`, `"velocity"` and `"mass"`.

- **identity** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Identity string of the realization. Sampler.sample derives the
identity string from the sampler’s identity string, the number of
particles and the seed.

- **parent** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Identity string of the sampler that the particles were drawn from.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If position or velocity does not have the shape (n, 3), with n
    the length of mass.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If component does not have the shape (n,), or holds an index that
    is negative or not below the number of component_names.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If unit_system is not `"internal"`, `"model"` or
    `"physical"`.

See also

[`Sampler.sample`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Sampler.sample)
Draw a Particles object from a model.

[`write_particles`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.write_particles)
Write particles to a file in a registered layout.

`read`
Read a file of the native layout back into a Particles object.

Notes

Two realizations hold identical particles when the two identity strings
are equal.

Examples

```python
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> particles = pp.Particles(
...     position=np.zeros((2, 3)),
...     velocity=np.ones((2, 3)),
...     mass=np.full(2, 0.5),
...     component=np.zeros(2, dtype=int),
...     component_names=("halo",),
...     unit_system="internal",
...     units={
...         "position": "internal", "velocity": "internal", "mass": "internal"
...     },
...     identity="a" * 64,
...     parent="b" * 64,
... )
>>> len(particles), particles.position.shape
(2, (2, 3))
```

write(*path*, *layout='native'*, ***options*)

Write the particles to a file in a registered layout.

`particles.write(path, layout, **options)` is the call
`write_particles(particles, path, layout, **options)`.

Parameters:

- **path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* or **path-like*) – Path of the file to write.

- **layout** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*, **optional*) – Name of a layout registered in `PARTICLE_WRITERS`: `"native"`,
`"gamer"`, `"gadget"`, `"text"`, or a name added by
register_particle_writer. Default: `"native"`, which means
the package’s own HDF5 result file.

- ****options** – Keyword options of the layout’s writer. write_particles lists
the options of every layout with their defaults.

Returns:

The file is written, read back and compared with the particles
before the call returns.

Return type:

None

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If layout is not registered in `PARTICLE_WRITERS`.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If an option’s value is outside the values the layout’s writer
    takes (write_particles lists the conditions).

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the file exists and the option `overwrite` is not true.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the file read back differs from the particles written.

See also

[`write_particles`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.write_particles)
The function that Particles.write calls.

`read`
Read a file of the native layout back into a Particles object.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> particles = pp.Particles(
...     position=np.zeros((2, 3)),
...     velocity=np.ones((2, 3)),
...     mass=np.full(2, 0.5),
...     component=np.zeros(2, dtype=int),
...     component_names=("halo",),
...     unit_system="internal",
...     units={"position": "r_0", "velocity": "v_W", "mass": "M_W"},
...     identity="a" * 64,
...     parent="b" * 64,
... )
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "halo.txt")
...     particles.write(path, layout="text")
...     with open(path) as file:
...         n_lines = len(file.readlines())
>>> n_lines
9
```

class pianistpy.particles.Sampler(*model*, *r_sample=None*, *r_range=None*)

The sampling tables of a model, built once, from which particles are drawn.

A Sampler builds the radius table, the velocity table and the angle table
of a model when the Sampler is created. Every call of Sampler.sample
and of Sampler.velocities reuses the three tables. For many draws from one
model, build one Sampler and call Sampler.sample on the one Sampler
for each draw.

Parameters:

- **model** ([*Model*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)) – The model to draw from: a model of one component, or a superposition
returned by superpose.

- **r_sample** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Outer radius of the sampling, in internal units whatever the model’s
unit system. r_sample must lie inside the radii of the model’s
profile. A model that is not spatially finite needs r_sample, and a
spatially finite model takes no r_sample. Default: `None`, which
means the truncation radius of a spatially finite model.

- **r_range** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)* of *[*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Radii (r_lo, r_hi) between which every particle is drawn, in internal
units, with r_lo and r_hi finite, `0 <= r_lo < r_hi` and r_hi at
most the outer radius of the sampling. Each particle’s radius is
drawn from the model’s enclosed mass restricted to the range, so
every particle lies in the range and the particles carry the mass of
the model between r_lo and r_hi. Each particle’s velocity and
directions take the random numbers of the draw without r_range.
Default: `None`, which means radii from the center to the outer
radius of the sampling.

Variables:

- **validation** ([*ValidationReport*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/validation#pianistpy.validation.ValidationReport)) – The report of the sampler: the velocity table’s checks `row_error` and
`polish_residual`, and the model’s own report as the parent
report. The report’s tier is the band of the largest relative error:
`"silent"` at or below \(10^{-6}\), `"recorded"` above
\(10^{-6}\) and at or below \(10^{-4}\), `"warned"` above
\(10^{-4}\) and at or below \(10^{-2}\), and `"refused"`
above \(10^{-2}\). A sampler whose tier is `"recorded"` writes
one line at level INFO to the package’s log. A sampler whose tier is
`"warned"` or `"refused"` also issues an AccuracyWarning.

- **identity** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Identity string of the sampler, derived from the model’s identity
string, r_sample, r_range, the settings and the package version.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If model is not a Model.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If model has more than one component and is not a superposition.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If r_sample is given for a spatially finite model, is missing for a
    model that is not spatially finite, or lies outside the radii of the
    model’s profile.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If r_range is not two finite radii with `0 <= r_lo < r_hi`, if r_hi
    is beyond the outer radius of the sampling, if r_hi is at or below the
    innermost radius of the radius table, or if r_lo is at or above the
    outermost radius of the radius table.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the model’s tier is `"refused"` and the model’s settings do not
    set `write_anyway=True` (Settings).

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If a check of the velocity table exceeds \(10^{-2}\) and the settings
    do not set `write_anyway=True`. With `write_anyway=True`, the
    Sampler is built with the tier `"refused"` and issues an
    AccuracyWarning.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the velocity table cannot resolve the distribution of velocity at a
    potential with the resolution that the settings allow.

- [**UnphysicalModelError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.UnphysicalModelError) – If the DF below the DF table’s lowest energy falls so steeply toward
    \(\mathcal{K} = 0\) that the mass at energies below the DF table’s
    lowest energy is not finite.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If a sampling table fails the table’s own consistency check: an
    inverse that is not finite and increasing, or a cumulative
    distribution that is not monotone.

See also

[`Sampler.sample`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Sampler.sample)
Draw particles from the model.

[`Sampler.velocities`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Sampler.velocities)
Draw one velocity at each user-specified 3D radius.

[`Particles`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Particles)
The result of Sampler.sample.

`superpose`
Build a superposition, which a Sampler also takes.

Notes

A model with a non-negative DF is not necessarily sampled within
\(10^{-4}\). The velocity table doubles the velocity table’s resolution
until the velocity table’s own error is below the setting
`sampling["row_error_goal"]` (\(10^{-6}\) with the default
settings, \(10^{-4}\) with the quick settings) or until the
resolution reaches the setting `sampling["n_rows_max"]`. For an
Osipkov-Merritt or Cuddeford-Osipkov-Merritt (COM) Type I DF whose
anisotropy radius \(R_{\rm a}\) is close to the smallest anisotropy
radius at which the DF is non-negative, the resolution reaches
`sampling["n_rows_max"]` first, and the velocity table’s error grows as
\(R_{\rm a}\) decreases toward the smallest anisotropy radius with a
non-negative DF. The report in
validation gives the velocity table’s error for each model. The page on
particles in the user guide lists, for each anisotropy model, the
anisotropy radius at which the velocity table’s error exceeds
\(10^{-4}\) and \(10^{-2}\).

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> model = pp.solve(
...     pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()),
...     settings=pp.Settings(quick=True),
... )
>>> sampler = pp.Sampler(model, r_sample=100.0)
>>> particles = sampler.sample(1000, seed=1)
>>> particles.position.shape, particles.unit_system
((1000, 3), 'internal')
```

sample(*n*, *seed=0*)

Return n equal-mass particles drawn from the model.

Each particle is determined by the seed, the particle’s component and
the particle’s index, and not by the number of particles requested.

Parameters:

- **n** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of particles, from 1 to \(2^{31} - 1\). A larger
number of particles is drawn in several calls with distinct seeds.

- **seed** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, **optional*) – Seed of the random numbers. One seed gives identical particles for
every value of the setting `sampling["draw_block"]`
(Settings). Default: `0`.

Returns:

**particles** – The n particles, in the unit system of the model (Model.to).
Every particle has the mass \(M_{\rm s}/n\), where
\(M_{\rm s}\) is the model’s mass inside the outer radius of
the sampling, or between r_lo and r_hi when the Sampler has an
r_range. The draw is made in internal units, and the positions,
velocities and masses are converted to the model’s unit system
at the output.

Return type:

[Particles](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Particles)

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If n is not a positive integer.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If n is \(2^{31}\) or more.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If a particle lies outside the phase-space support of the
    particle’s component, or if the velocity rebuilt from the
    particle’s arrays misses the support’s bound by more than the
    rounding of the particle’s own variables.

See also

[`Sampler.velocities`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Sampler.velocities)
Draw one velocity at each user-specified 3D radius.

[`write_particles`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.write_particles)
Write the particles to a file.

Examples

```python
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> model = pp.solve(
...     pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()),
...     settings=pp.Settings(quick=True),
... )
>>> particles = pp.Sampler(model, r_sample=100.0).sample(1000, seed=1)
>>> len(particles), bool(np.all(particles.mass == particles.mass[0]))
(1000, True)
```

velocities(*r*, *seed=0*, *v_range=None*)

Return one velocity drawn at each user-specified 3D radius, within a
user-specified range of velocities.

Parameters:

- **r** (*array-like**, **shape** (**n**,**)*) – User-specified 3D radii, in internal units whatever the model’s
unit system. Every radius is finite, positive and at most the outer
radius of the sampling.

- **seed** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, **optional*) – Seed of the random numbers. The velocity at the i-th radius takes the
velocity’s random number of particle i of Sampler.sample at the
same seed, mapped into the user-specified range. For a
superposition, the component of the i-th velocity is chosen with
probabilities proportional to each component’s weight times the
component’s fraction of velocities in the range. Default: `0`.

- **v_range** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)* of *[*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **of array-like**, **optional*) – The user-specified range of velocities (v_lo, v_hi), in internal
units, with v_lo finite, v_hi finite or infinite, and
`0 <= v_lo < v_hi`. Each bound is a float, which applies at
every radius, or an array that broadcasts against r, which
gives a bound at each radius (for example, a bound in units of
each radius’s escape velocity). Default: `None`, which means the
velocities from 0 to infinity, the whole distribution of velocity.

Returns:

- **v** (*array, shape (n,)*) – The velocity at each radius of r, in internal units, drawn from the
model’s distribution of velocity at the radius, restricted to the
user-specified range. The velocity is NaN at a radius where the
user-specified range holds no part of the distribution of velocity.

- **fraction** (*array, shape (n,)*) – The fraction of the distribution of velocity at each radius that
lies in the user-specified range. For a superposition, the
fraction is the sum over components of each component’s weight
times the component’s fraction.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a component has a finite anisotropy radius (Osipkov-Merritt
    or Cuddeford-Osipkov-Merritt). For such a component the velocity is
    the scaled velocity times a factor of the drawn angle, so the
    user-specified range of velocities depends on the angle, and no table
    holds the distribution of velocity at a radius with the angle
    integrated out.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If r is not one-dimensional, or a radius in r is not finite,
    not positive or beyond the outer radius of the sampling.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If v_range is not two bounds, or if v_lo is not finite, v_hi is
    NaN or `0 <= v_lo < v_hi` fails at a radius.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the bounds of v_range do not broadcast against r.

Return type:

[tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), [*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

See also

[`Sampler.sample`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Sampler.sample)
Draw particles, positions and velocities included.

Examples

```python
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> model = pp.solve(
...     pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()),
...     settings=pp.Settings(quick=True),
... )
>>> sampler = pp.Sampler(model, r_sample=100.0)
>>> v, frac = sampler.velocities([0.5, 1.0, 2.0], seed=1, v_range=(0.1, 0.3))
>>> v.shape, bool(np.all((frac > 0.0) & (frac < 1.0)))
((3,), True)
```

pianistpy.particles.component_view(*model*, *k*)

Return component k of a superposed model as a model of one component.

Sampler and the observables read each component of a superposition
through component_view.

Parameters:

- **model** ([*Model*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)) – A superposed model, for which is_superposition returns True.

- **k** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Index of the component, from 0 to the number of components of
model minus one.

Returns:

**view** – A model of one component: component k with mass 1, component k’s DF
table on component k’s own energy grid, and the truncated profile
that the components of model share. component_view raises no
package exception for a superposed model and a valid k.

Return type:

[Model](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)

See also

[`is_superposition`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.is_superposition)
Test whether a model is a superposition.

`superpose`
Build a superposition.

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> from pianistpy.particles import component_view
>>> parent = pp.solve(
...     pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()), pp.Truncation(k_t=0.05)
... )
>>> children = [
...     pp.solve(pp.Component(parent.profile, pp.Anisotropy(beta_c=beta_c)))
...     for beta_c in (0.0, 0.2)
... ]
>>> composite = pp.superpose({children[0]: 0.5, children[1]: 0.5})
>>> view = component_view(composite, 1)
>>> len(composite.components), len(view.components)
(2, 1)
```

pianistpy.particles.is_superposition(*model*)

Return whether every component of a model shares one truncated profile.

A model returned by superpose shares one truncated profile across the
model’s components. A model of one component on a truncated profile also
passes the test; Sampler treats a model as a superposition only when
the model has more than one component.

Parameters:

**model** ([*Model*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)) – The model to test.

Returns:

**superposed** – True if the first component’s profile is a truncated profile and
every other component’s profile equals the first component’s
profile; False otherwise. is_superposition raises no package
exception.

Return type:

[bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

See also

`superpose`
Build a superposition from models on one truncated profile.

[`component_view`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.component_view)
One component of a superposition as a model.

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> from pianistpy.particles import is_superposition
>>> model = pp.solve(pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()))
>>> is_superposition(model)
False
```

pianistpy.particles.register_particle_writer(*layout*)

Return a decorator that registers a function as the writer of a layout.

The decorated function becomes the writer that write_particles and
Particles.write call for the name layout. A writer takes the
particles, the path of the file and the writer’s own keyword options. A
file layout of another simulation code is added by one registered
function, with no change to Sampler or to Particles.

Parameters:

**layout** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Name of the layout, as passed to write_particles.

Returns:

**decorator** – A decorator that adds the decorated function to `PARTICLE_WRITERS`
under the name layout and returns the function unchanged.

Return type:

callable

Raises:

[**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If `PARTICLE_WRITERS` already holds a writer under the name
    layout. The decorator raises the error when the decorator is
    applied to a function.

See also

[`write_particles`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.write_particles)
Write particles in a registered layout.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy.particles import PARTICLE_WRITERS, register_particle_writer
>>> @register_particle_writer("count_only")
... def write_count(particles, path, overwrite=False):
...     with open(path, "w") as file:
...         file.write(str(len(particles)))
>>> "count_only" in PARTICLE_WRITERS
True
>>> del PARTICLE_WRITERS["count_only"]
```

pianistpy.particles.write_particles(*particles*, *path*, *layout='native'*, ***options*)

Write particles to a file in a registered layout.

Every writer reads the file back after writing the file and compares the
values read with the particles. The comparison is bit for bit after the
cast to the file’s number type, and to the 14 digits written after the
decimal point for the `"text"` layout.

Parameters:

- **particles** ([*Particles*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Particles)) – The particles to write.

- **path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* or **path-like*) – Path of the file to write.

- **layout** (*{"native"**, **"gamer"**, **"gadget"**, **"text"}** or *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*, **optional*) – Name of a layout registered in `PARTICLE_WRITERS`.

- `"native"`: the package’s own HDF5 result file, which read
reads back into a Particles object.

- `"gamer"`: the particle file that GAMER reads at its
initialization from file (`PAR_INIT 3`), a stream of the
particle attributes with no header.

- `"gadget"`: a Gadget-derivative HDF5 initial condition in
snapshot format 3, with the groups and attributes of the
OpenGadget3 reference example.

- `"text"`: fixed-width text with a header that states the unit
of every column.

- any other name: a layout added by register_particle_writer.

Default: `"native"`, which means the package’s own HDF5 result
file.

- ****options** – Keyword options of the layout’s writer. Every option is optional.

- Every layout takes `overwrite` (bool). Default: `False`, which
means an existing file at path is not replaced.

- `"gamer"` takes `order` (`"ATT_ID"` or `"ID_ATT"`): one
block per attribute (every particle’s mass, then every particle’s
x, and so on) for `"ATT_ID"`, or one record per particle for
`"ID_ATT"`, the two values that GAMER’s parameter
`PAR_IC_FORMAT` takes. Default: `"ATT_ID"`.

- `"gamer"` takes `double_precision` (bool): float64 values for a
GAMER build with `PAR_IC_FLOAT8`, float32 values otherwise.
Default: `True`.

- `"gamer"` takes `include_mass` (bool): false for a GAMER run
that sets the particle mass itself (`PAR_IC_MASS` at or above
zero). Default: `True`.

- `"gamer"` takes `offset` (array-like, shape (3,)): a vector
added to every position, because GAMER’s simulation box has its
corner at the origin while the sampler centers the model at the
origin. Default: `None`, which means no shift.

- `"gamer"` takes `attributes` (`"standard"` or `"legacy"`):
`"standard"` writes the mass, the position and the velocity.
`"legacy"` writes 13 float32 blocks, one per attribute, in the
layout of the GAMER build used for the runs of [Chiang+(2026d)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28758): the
mass, the position, the velocity, the type 1, the tag 1, the
energy 0, the angular momentum 0, the energy backup 0 and the
identifiers 0 to \(n - 1\). Default: `"standard"`.

- `"gadget"` takes `double_precision` (bool): float64 arrays and
the header flag `Flag_DoublePrecision` set to 1, or float32
arrays and the flag set to 0. Default: `False`.

- `"gadget"` takes `part_type` (int): the particle type slot,
from 0 to 5. Default: `1`.

- `"gadget"` takes `hubble_param` (float): the value written to
the header’s `HubbleParam`, which an isolated model does not
use. Default: `0.7`.

- `"gadget"` takes `offset` (array-like, shape (3,)): a vector
added to every position. Default: `None`, which means no shift.

- `"native"` and `"text"` take `overwrite` only.

The `"gadget"` writer puts equal particle masses into the header’s
mass table and writes unequal masses per particle. The `"text"`
header states the unit system, the unit of every column, the
identity strings and the column names. Each line of the `"text"`
file holds the mass, the position and the velocity of one particle,
followed by the particle’s component index when the particles have
more than one component.

Returns:

The file is written, read back and compared with the particles
before the call returns.

Return type:

None

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If layout is not registered in `PARTICLE_WRITERS`.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the file exists and the option `overwrite` is not true.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – For `"gamer"`, if `order` is not `"ATT_ID"` or `"ID_ATT"`,
    or `attributes` is not `"standard"` or `"legacy"`.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – For `"gamer"` or `"gadget"`, if `offset` does not have the
    shape (3,).

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – For `"gamer"` with `attributes="legacy"`, if `order`,
    `double_precision` or `include_mass` differs from its default.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – For `"gamer"` with `attributes="legacy"`, if the number of
    particles exceeds \(2^{24}\), the largest integer that a float32
    identifier holds exactly.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – For `"gadget"`, if `part_type` is not an integer from 0 to 5.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the file read back differs from the particles written.

See also

[`Particles.write`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.Particles.write)
write_particles as a method of Particles.

[`register_particle_writer`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/particles#pianistpy.particles.register_particle_writer)
Add a layout to `PARTICLE_WRITERS`.

`read`
Read a file of the native layout back into a Particles object.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> from pianistpy.particles import write_particles
>>> particles = pp.Particles(
...     position=np.zeros((2, 3)),
...     velocity=np.ones((2, 3)),
...     mass=np.full(2, 0.5),
...     component=np.zeros(2, dtype=int),
...     component_names=("halo",),
...     unit_system="internal",
...     units={"position": "r_0", "velocity": "v_W", "mass": "M_W"},
...     identity="a" * 64,
...     parent="b" * 64,
... )
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "halo.txt")
...     write_particles(particles, path, layout="text")
...     with open(path) as file:
...         first_line = file.readline().strip()
>>> first_line
'# PIANISTpy particles'
```


---

# Observables

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables

Module `pianistpy.observables`

Velocity dispersions and velocity distributions of a model.

The functions of pianistpy.observables return the radial, tangential and
line-of-sight velocity dispersions, the line-of-sight velocity distribution,
and the local velocity distribution of a model, at user-specified radii or in a
user-specified aperture on the plane of the sky.

class pianistpy.observables.Aperture(*shape*, *r_off=0.0*, *r_ape=None*, *side_x=None*, *side_y=None*, *angle=0.0*)

An aperture on the plane of the sky, circular or rectangular.

The constructors Aperture.circle and Aperture.rectangle build an
aperture. The lengths of an aperture are in the unit system of the
model or LosTable that the aperture is used with. In the internal and
the model systems, the unit of length is the scale radius \(r_0\).
In the physical system, the unit of length is the parsec.

Parameters:

- **shape** (*{"circle"**, **"rectangle"}*) – Shape of the aperture. `"circle"` is a circle of radius r_ape.
`"rectangle"` is a rectangle of full sides side_x and side_y.

- **r_off** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Projected distance \(R_{\rm off}\) of the center of the aperture
from the center of the model. r_off must be zero or positive.
Default: `0.0`, which means the aperture is centered on the model.

- **r_ape** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Radius \(R_{\rm ape}\) of a circle. r_ape must be positive for
a circle and must be `None` for a rectangle. Default: `None`.

- **side_x** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Full length of the rectangle’s side along the rectangle’s x axis.
side_x must be positive for a rectangle and must be `None` for a
circle. Default: `None`.

- **side_y** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Full length of the rectangle’s side along the rectangle’s y axis.
side_y must be positive for a rectangle and must be `None` for a
circle. Default: `None`.

- **angle** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Angle, in radians, between the rectangle’s x axis and the line
through the center of the model and the center of the rectangle.
Default: `0.0`, which means the rectangle’s x axis lies on the
line through the center of the model and the center of the
rectangle. A circle accepts only `0.0`.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If shape is neither `"circle"` nor `"rectangle"`.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If r_off is negative.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a length the shape requires is missing or not positive.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a length the shape does not use is given, or a circle is given a
    nonzero angle.

See also

[`sigma_los_aperture`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.sigma_los_aperture)
Line-of-sight velocity dispersion inside an aperture.

[`aperture_losvd`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.aperture_losvd)
Line-of-sight velocity distribution inside an aperture.

Examples

```python
>>> Aperture.circle(1.0, r_off=10.0).shape
'circle'
>>> Aperture.rectangle(2.0, 0.5, r_off=10.0, angle=0.3).side_y
0.5
```

classmethod circle(*r_ape*, *r_off=0.0*)

Parameters:

positive.

- **r_off** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – Projected distance \(R_{\rm off}\) of the circle’s center
from the center of the model. r_off must be zero or positive.
Default: `0.0`, which means the circle is centered on the
model.

Returns:

**aperture** – The circular aperture. The lengths r_ape and r_off are in
the unit system of the model that the aperture is used with.

[Aperture](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Aperture)

Raises:

classmethod rectangle(*side_x*, *side_y*, *r_off=0.0*, *angle=0.0*)

A circular aperture.

arc(*r*)

Return the angle, in radians, of the circle of radius r inside
the aperture.

The circle of radius r is centered on the model. The angle
\({\rm arc}(r)\) is \(2\pi\) where the whole circle lies
inside the aperture. The angle is zero where no part of the circle
lies inside the aperture. The integral over the aperture of a
quantity \(f(R)\) of projected radius is
\(\int f(R)\,{\rm arc}(R)\,R\,{\rm d}R\).

Parameters:

**r** (*array-like*) – User-specified projected radii, zero or positive, in the unit of
length of the aperture.

Returns:

**arc** – The angle \({\rm arc}(r)\) in radians, from zero to
\(2\pi\), with the shape of r.

Return type:

array

See also

[`Aperture.breaks`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Aperture.breaks)
The projected radii at which \({\rm arc}(r)\) is not smooth.

Notes

For a circle of radius \(R_{\rm ape}\) at offset
\(R_{\rm off} > 0\), the angle is \(2\pi\) for
\(r \le R_{\rm ape} - R_{\rm off}\), zero for
\(r < |R_{\rm off} - R_{\rm ape}|\) or
\(r > R_{\rm off} + R_{\rm ape}\), and otherwise

\[{\rm arc}(r) = 4 \arcsin\sqrt{x/2}, \qquad
x = \frac{R_{\rm ape}^2 - (r - R_{\rm off})^2}{2 r R_{\rm off}}.\]

For a centered circle (\(R_{\rm off} = 0\)), the angle is
\(2\pi\) for \(r \le R_{\rm ape}\) and zero otherwise.

For a rectangle, each of the rectangle’s four edge lines crosses
the circle of radius r at angles given in closed form. These
crossing angles cut the circle into arcs. Each arc lies wholly
inside or wholly outside the rectangle. The angle
\({\rm arc}(r)\) is the sum of the arcs inside the rectangle.
The same closed form holds for a rectangle that contains the center
of the model, a rectangle whose edge passes through the center of
the model, and a rectangle that excludes the center of the model.

breaks()

Return the projected radii at which Aperture.arc is not smooth.

A quadrature in projected radius whose intervals end at the returned
projected radii integrates a smooth function on each interval.

Returns:

**breaks** – The positive projected radii, in increasing order and in the
unit of length of the aperture. For a centered circle, the
list holds \(R_{\rm ape}\). For an offset circle, the list
holds the positive values among
\(|R_{\rm off} - R_{\rm ape}|\),
\(R_{\rm ape} - R_{\rm off}\) and
\(R_{\rm off} + R_{\rm ape}\). For a rectangle, the list
holds at most eight projected radii. Four of the eight are the
distances from the center of the model to the rectangle’s four
edge lines. Each such distance is included only where the point
of the edge line nearest to the center of the model lies on the
edge. The other four are the distances from the center of the
model to the rectangle’s four corners.

Return type:

[list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list) of [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

See also

[`Aperture.arc`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Aperture.arc)
The angle of the circle of radius r inside the aperture.

class pianistpy.observables.Differentiable(*model*, *settings=None*)

The observables of a one-component model as JAX functions of the
component’s anisotropy.

The anisotropy is the pair \(\theta = (\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of
the central anisotropy \(\beta_{\rm c}\) and the anisotropy radius
\(R_{\rm a}\). Each method of Differentiable takes \(\theta\) as
the first argument. Each method returns the value of the public function
of the same name as the method (pianistpy.sigma_los for
Differentiable.sigma_los) on the model rebuilt at \(\theta\). Each method is a
JAX function of \(\theta\) and works under `jax.jit` and
`jax.grad`. To differentiate the observables of a model with several
components, call likelihood.

Parameters:

- **model** ([*Model*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)) – Model of one component. The model must meet three conditions: the
model is spatially finite (`model.spatially_finite` is True); the
component’s profile is the truncated profile of a parent model and
carries the parent’s distribution function (DF); and the component’s
anisotropy family is isotropic, constant, Osipkov-Merritt (OM) Type
I, OM Type II or Cuddeford-Osipkov-Merritt (COM) Type I.

- **settings** ([*Settings*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings#pianistpy.settings.Settings)*, **optional*) – Numerical settings of the observables. Default: `None`, which
means the settings of model.

Variables:

- **model** ([*Model*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)) – The model passed to the constructor.

- **theta** (*array**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – The anisotropy \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of the model’s
component. \(\beta_{\rm c}\) is dimensionless. \(R_{\rm a}\)
is in internal units in every unit system of the model (internal,
model and physical). An isotropic or constant component has an
infinite \(R_{\rm a}\).

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If model is not a Model, or if model has more than one
    component. The components of a model with several components are
    differentiated through likelihood.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the model is not spatially finite, or if the component’s profile
    is not a truncated profile that carries the DF of a parent model.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the component’s anisotropy family is COM Type II. The observables
    of a COM Type II component are not differentiable in the anisotropy.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a setting of the `observables` group is outside the setting’s
    range: `n_projection_nodes` below 20.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the validation report of the model has tier `"refused"` (an
    error above \(10^{-2}\)) and the settings of the model do not set
    `write_anyway=True`.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the squared line-of-sight dispersion of the model is negative at
    a tabulated projected radius.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If an intermediate result fails a check that the next step of the
    computation needs, for example non-finite values from a degenerate
    model.

See also

`likelihood`
The likelihood of data given a model, differentiable in the anisotropy of each component.

`truncate`
The truncated model whose profile a differentiable component uses.

[`sigma_los`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.sigma_los)
The line-of-sight velocity dispersion of a model.

[`losvd`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.losvd)
The line-of-sight velocity distribution of a model.

[`pdf_v`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.pdf_v)
The local velocity distribution of a model.

Notes

Every radius, velocity, aperture length and \(R_{\rm a}\) that a
method reads is in internal units in every unit system of the model.
Every value that a method returns is in internal units.

The first call of a method at a new \(\theta\) inverts the DF of the
component at \(\theta\) on the component’s truncated profile. The
first call then builds the tables of the observable at \(\theta\). A
Differentiable keeps the tables of at most eight values of
\(\theta\): the model’s own \(\theta\) and the seven other values
of \(\theta\) first met most recently.

At a \(\theta\) where rebuilding the model raises InputError,
UnphysicalModelError, AccuracyError or ResultError, a method
returns NaN and a zero gradient. Any other package error raised during
the computation of a method reaches the caller as
`jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError`. The message of the
`jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` carries the message of the package error.
Three checks run before the computation and raise the package error
directly: the check of a concrete radius against the tabulated radii in
sigma_r, sigma_t and sigma_los; the check that the component’s DF
is differentiable in losvd, pdf_v and aperture_losvd; and the
check that the aperture passed to aperture_losvd is an Aperture.

The derivative of a method holds fixed the radii and velocities at which
the tables at \(\theta\) are tabulated. The value of a method follows
the change of the tabulated radii and velocities from one \(\theta\)
to another. The derivative of a method omits the change of the tabulated
radii and velocities. A method is not differentiable in the radii or
velocities that the method reads. The gradient in a radius or a velocity
is NaN.

The parameters that carry a derivative depend on the method:

- sigma_r, sigma_t, sigma_los and sigma_los_aperture carry the
derivative in \(\beta_{\rm c}\) for every accepted family, and in
\(R_{\rm a}\) for the OM and COM families.

- losvd, pdf_v and aperture_losvd carry the derivative in
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) for the constant and COM Type I families, and in
\(R_{\rm a}\) for the OM and COM Type I families. The gradient of
losvd, pdf_v or aperture_losvd in \(\beta_{\rm c}\) is NaN
for an OM component.

- For an isotropic or constant component, every method holds
\(R_{\rm a}\) at infinity, and the gradient in \(R_{\rm a}\) is
zero.

References

Notes Section T:7.2. Notes Section T:7.3.

Examples

```python
>>> import jax
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> parent = pp.truncate(
...     pp.compute_df(pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist(), pp.Anisotropy())),
...     pp.Truncation(k_t=0.05),
... )
>>> member = pp.truncate(
...     pp.compute_df(
...         pp.Component(
...             profile=parent.profile, anisotropy=pp.Anisotropy(beta_c=0.25)
...         )
...     )
... )
>>> d = pp.Differentiable(member)
>>> grad = jax.grad(lambda theta: d.sigma_los(theta, [0.1, 0.3]).sum())(d.theta)
>>> grad.shape
(2,)
```

sigma_r(*theta*, *r*)

Return the radial velocity dispersion at user-specified 3D radii
for the model at the anisotropy theta.

The value is pianistpy.sigma_r of the model rebuilt at theta.

Parameters:

- **theta** (*array-like**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – Anisotropy \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of the component.
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) is dimensionless. \(R_{\rm a}\) is in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **r** (*array-like*) – User-specified 3D radii \(r\). The radii are in internal units
in every unit system of the model.

Returns:

**sigma_r** – Radial velocity dispersion \(\sigma_{\rm r}\) in internal
units, with the shape of r. Every value is NaN when rebuilding
the model at theta raises InputError, UnphysicalModelError,
AccuracyError or ResultError.

Return type:

array

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a radius lies inside the innermost or beyond the outermost
    radius that the model tabulates. A radius inside a function
    compiled by `jax.jit` is not checked before the computation.

- [**jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError**](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/101/errors.html#jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError) – If the computation raises a package error other than the four
    package errors that give NaN, for example
    pianistpy.exceptions.WorkerError when a parallel process ends.
    The message of the `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` carries the
    message of the package error.

See also

[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

sigma_los(*theta*, *r_2d*)

Return the line-of-sight velocity dispersion at user-specified
projected radii for the model at the anisotropy theta.

The value is pianistpy.sigma_los of the model rebuilt at theta.

Parameters:

- **theta** (*array-like**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – Anisotropy \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of the component.
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) is dimensionless. \(R_{\rm a}\) is in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **r_2d** (*array-like*) – User-specified projected radii \(R_{\rm 2D}\). The projected
radii are in internal units in every unit system of the model.

Returns:

**sigma_los** – Line-of-sight velocity dispersion \(\sigma_{\rm los}\) in
internal units, with the shape of r_2d. Every value is NaN when
rebuilding the model at theta raises InputError,
UnphysicalModelError, AccuracyError or ResultError.

Return type:

array

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a projected radius lies inside the innermost or beyond the
    outermost projected radius that the model tabulates. A projected
    radius inside a function compiled by `jax.jit` is not checked
    before the computation.

- [**jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError**](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/101/errors.html#jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError) – If the computation raises a package error other than the four
    package errors that give NaN, for example
    pianistpy.exceptions.WorkerError when a parallel process ends.
    The message of the `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` carries the
    message of the package error.

See also

[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)
The line-of-sight velocity dispersion of a model.

[`Differentiable.sigma_los_aperture`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Differentiable.sigma_los_aperture)
The line-of-sight velocity dispersion over an aperture as a JAX function of the anisotropy.

sigma_los_aperture(*theta*, *aperture*)

Return the line-of-sight velocity dispersion over an aperture for
the model at the anisotropy theta.

The aperture dispersion \(\sigma_{\rm ape}\) is the root mean
square of \(\sigma_{\rm los}\) over the aperture, weighted by the
surface density. The value is pianistpy.sigma_los_aperture of the
model rebuilt at theta.

Parameters:

- **theta** (*array-like**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – Anisotropy \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of the component.
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) is dimensionless. \(R_{\rm a}\) is in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **aperture** ([*Aperture*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Aperture)) – User-specified aperture. The lengths of the aperture are in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

Returns:

**sigma_los** – Aperture dispersion \(\sigma_{\rm ape}\) in internal units.
The value is NaN when rebuilding the model at theta raises
InputError, UnphysicalModelError, AccuracyError or ResultError.

Return type:

scalar array

Raises:

[**jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError**](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/101/errors.html#jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError) – If pianistpy.sigma_los_aperture raises InputError for the
    aperture on the model at theta, because the tables of the model
    do not cover the aperture. The message of the
    `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` carries the message of the
    InputError.

See also

`pianistpy.sigma_los_aperture`
The line-of-sight velocity dispersion of a model over an aperture.

[`Aperture`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Aperture)
The apertures of the observables.

[`Differentiable.aperture_losvd`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Differentiable.aperture_losvd)
The line-of-sight velocity distribution in an aperture as a JAX function of the anisotropy.

Notes

The derivative of \(\sigma_{\rm ape}\) in a parameter
\(\theta_i\) (\(\beta_{\rm c}\) or \(R_{\rm a}\)) is

\[\frac{\partial \sigma_{\rm ape}}{\partial \theta_i}
= \frac{1}{2\sigma_{\rm ape}}
\frac{\int_A \Sigma\, \partial \sigma_{\rm los}^2/\partial
\theta_i \, {\rm d}A}{\int_A \Sigma \, {\rm d}A},\]

with \(A\) the aperture and \(\Sigma\) the surface density of
the component. The surface density does not depend on
\(\theta\), since the component’s profile is fixed. Both
integrals use the quadrature nodes and weights of
pianistpy.sigma_los_aperture.

losvd(*theta*, *r_2d*, *v*)

Return the line-of-sight velocity distribution at the pairs
`(r_2d, v)` for the model at the anisotropy theta.

The value is pianistpy.losvd of the model rebuilt at theta.

Parameters:

- **theta** (*array-like**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – Anisotropy \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of the component.
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) is dimensionless. \(R_{\rm a}\) is in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **r_2d** (*array-like*) – User-specified projected radii \(R_{\rm 2D}\). The projected
radii are in internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **v** (*array-like*) – Line-of-sight velocities \(V\), in internal units in every
unit system of the model. The arrays r_2d and v broadcast
against each other.

Returns:

**losvd** – Line-of-sight velocity distribution per unit internal velocity,
with the broadcast shape of r_2d and v. Every value is NaN
when rebuilding the model at theta raises InputError,
UnphysicalModelError, AccuracyError or ResultError.

Return type:

array

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the component’s DF is not differentiable in the anisotropy.
    The DF of an isotropic component is not differentiable in the
    anisotropy. The DF of a component whose DF center lies on a
    critical branch is not differentiable in the anisotropy. The
    message states the reason.

- [**jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError**](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/101/errors.html#jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError) – If the computation raises a package error other than the four
    package errors that give NaN, for example
    pianistpy.exceptions.WorkerError when a parallel process ends.
    The message of the `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` carries the
    message of the package error. A projected radius outside the
    table, for which pianistpy.losvd raises a package error, gives
    a `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError`.

See also

`pianistpy.losvd`
The line-of-sight velocity distribution of a model.

[`Differentiable.aperture_losvd`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Differentiable.aperture_losvd)
The line-of-sight velocity distribution in an aperture as a JAX function of the anisotropy.

Notes

The derivative in a parameter \(\theta_i\) (\(\beta_{\rm c}\)
or \(R_{\rm a}\)) is the sum of two parts. The first part is the
derivative in \(\theta_i\) at a fixed DF table. The second part
is the derivative through the values of the DF table, with the
energies of the DF table held fixed. The method is not
differentiable in r_2d or v.

References

Notes Section T:7.1.

pdf_v(*theta*, *r*, *v*)

Return the local velocity distribution at the pairs `(r, v)` for the
model at the anisotropy theta.

The value is pianistpy.pdf_v of the model rebuilt at theta.

Parameters:

- **theta** (*array-like**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – Anisotropy \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of the component.
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) is dimensionless. \(R_{\rm a}\) is in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **r** (*array-like*) – User-specified 3D radii \(r\). The radii are in internal units
in every unit system of the model.

- **v** (*array-like*) – Velocities \(v\), in internal units in every unit system of the
model. The arrays r and v broadcast against each other.

Returns:

**pdf_v** – Local velocity distribution per unit internal velocity, with the
broadcast shape of r and v. Every value is NaN when rebuilding
the model at theta raises InputError, UnphysicalModelError,
AccuracyError or ResultError.

Return type:

array

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the component’s DF is not differentiable in the anisotropy.
    The DF of an isotropic component is not differentiable in the
    anisotropy. The DF of a component whose DF center lies on a
    critical branch is not differentiable in the anisotropy. The
    message states the reason.

- [**jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError**](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/101/errors.html#jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError) – If the computation raises a package error other than the four
    package errors that give NaN, for example
    pianistpy.exceptions.WorkerError when a parallel process ends.
    The message of the `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` carries the
    message of the package error. A radius outside the radii of the
    model, for which pianistpy.pdf_v raises a package error, gives a
    `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError`.

See also

`pianistpy.pdf_v`
The local velocity distribution of a model.

[`Differentiable.losvd`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Differentiable.losvd)
The line-of-sight velocity distribution as a JAX function of the anisotropy.

Notes

The derivative in a parameter \(\theta_i\) (\(\beta_{\rm c}\)
or \(R_{\rm a}\)) is the sum of two parts. The first part is the
derivative in \(\theta_i\) at a fixed DF table and at fixed
velocities. The second part is the derivative through the values of the
DF table, with the energies of the DF table held fixed. The method is
not differentiable in r or v.

References

Notes Section T:7.1.

aperture_losvd(*theta*, *aperture*, *v*)

Return the line-of-sight velocity distribution in an aperture at
user-specified line-of-sight velocities for the model at the
anisotropy theta.

The value is pianistpy.aperture_losvd of the model rebuilt at
theta.

Parameters:

- **theta** (*array-like**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – Anisotropy \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\) of the component.
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) is dimensionless. \(R_{\rm a}\) is in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **aperture** ([*Aperture*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/observables#pianistpy.observables.Aperture)) – User-specified aperture. The lengths of the aperture are in
internal units in every unit system of the model.

- **v** (*array-like*) – Line-of-sight velocities \(V\), in internal units in every
unit system of the model.

Returns:

**losvd** – Line-of-sight velocity distribution in the aperture per unit
internal velocity, with the shape of v. Every value is NaN when
rebuilding the model at theta raises InputError,
UnphysicalModelError, AccuracyError or ResultError.

Return type:

array

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the component’s DF is not differentiable in the anisotropy.
    The DF of an isotropic component is not differentiable in the
    anisotropy. The DF of a component whose DF center lies on a
    critical branch is not differentiable in the anisotropy.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If aperture is not an Aperture.

- [**jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError**](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/101/errors.html#jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError) – If the computation raises a package error other than the four
    package errors that give NaN, for example
    pianistpy.exceptions.WorkerError when a parallel process ends.
    The message of the `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` carries the
    message of the package error. An aperture that the table does not
    cover, for which pianistpy.aperture_losvd raises a package
    error, gives a `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError`.

See also

`pianistpy.aperture_losvd`
The line-of-sight velocity distribution of a model in an aperture.

The derivative in a parameter \(\theta_i\) (\(\beta_{\rm c}\)
or \(R_{\rm a}\)) is the sum of two parts. The first part is the
derivative in \(\theta_i\) at a fixed DF table. The second part
is the derivative through the values of the DF table, with the
energies of the DF table held fixed. The method is not
differentiable in v.
