class pianistpy.inference.Likelihood(*tables*, *blocks*, *weights*, *scale*, *length*, *velocity*, *r_min*, *r_max*, *free=()*, *theta=None*, *members=()*, *readings=()*, *binned=()*)

The log-likelihood of a model against data, as a JAX function.

likelihood builds a Likelihood. A call of a Likelihood with the
component weights, the mass and length scales and, for free components,
the anisotropy parameters returns the Gaussian log-likelihood. JAX can
compile the call and differentiate the call in each argument.

Variables:

- **tables** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) – The projected table of each component, read in JAX.

- **blocks** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) – Each Data of dispersions or Gauss-Hermite moments, prepared.

- **weights** (*array**, **shape** (**n_components**,**)*) – The model’s own component weights, which are the masses of the
components.

- **scale** (*array**, **shape** (**2**,**)*) – The model’s own mass scale and length scale, in the units of the
data.

- **length** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The length factor \(L\) of the unit system of the data at the
model’s own scales.

- **velocity** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The velocity factor \(V\) of the unit system of the data at the
model’s own scales.

- **r_min** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The innermost projected radius of the tables, in internal units.

- **r_max** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The outermost projected radius of the tables, in internal units.

- **free** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)* of *[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – The indices of the components whose anisotropy parameters
(\(\beta_{\rm c}\), \(R_{\rm a}\)) are parameters of the
likelihood.

- **theta** (*array**, **shape** (**n_free**, **2**)*) – The model’s own (\(\beta_{\rm c}\), \(R_{\rm a}\)) of each
free component, in internal units.

- **members** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) – The free components, each with the tables computed at every
anisotropy at which the Likelihood has been called.

- **readings** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) – The squared line-of-sight dispersion \(\sigma_{\rm los}^2\) of
each free component, as a JAX function of the component’s
anisotropy parameters.

- **binned** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) – Each Data of `"losvd"`, `"losvd_aperture"` or `"pdf_v"`,
prepared.

Parameters:

- **tables** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*[**_Table**, **...**]*)

- **blocks** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*[**_Block** | **_Moments** | **_PointMoments**, **...**]*)

- **weights** ([*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any))

- **scale** ([*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any))

- **length** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float))

- **velocity** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float))

- **r_min** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float))

- **r_max** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float))

- **free** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*[*[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, **...**]*)

- **theta** ([*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)* | **None*)

- **members** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*[**_Free**, **...**]*)

- **readings** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*[*[*Any*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*, **...**]*)

- **binned** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)*[**_BinnedBlock**, **...**]*)

See also

[`likelihood`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.likelihood)
Build the Likelihood of a model against data.

[`log_likelihood`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.log_likelihood)
The log-likelihood at the model’s own weights and scales.

[`Data`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Data)
The measurements a Likelihood compares with.

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> model = pp.solve(pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()))
>>> data = pp.Data(
...     "sigma_los", [0.30, 0.25], r_2d=[0.5, 1.0], errors=[0.01, 0.01]
... )
>>> like = pp.likelihood(model, data)
>>> bool(float(like()) > float("-inf"))
True
>>> float(like(scale=[1.0, -1.0]))
-inf
```

pianistpy.inference.likelihood(*model*, *data*, *settings=None*, *free=()*)

Return the log-likelihood of a model against data, as a JAX function.

likelihood computes the projected table of each component once and
returns a Likelihood, which reads the tables in JAX at every call. A
model and data that cannot be compared raise an exception in
likelihood, never in a call of the returned Likelihood. For one
value at the model’s own weights and scales, call log_likelihood.

Parameters:

- **model** ([*Model*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)) – A model of one component, or a superposition (superpose), in the
unit system of the data.

- **data** ([*Data*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Data)* or **sequence** of *[*Data*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Data)) – The measurements. The log-likelihoods of several Data are summed.

- **settings** ([*Settings*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings#pianistpy.settings.Settings)*, **optional*) – The numerical settings of the observables. Default: `None`, which
means the model’s own settings.

- **free** (*sequence** of *[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, **optional*) – The indices of the components whose anisotropy parameters
(\(\beta_{\rm c}\), \(R_{\rm a}\)) become the parameter
`theta` of the returned Likelihood. Each free component is a
spatially finite Method II model: a DF computed on the truncated
profile of another model, where the truncated profile carries the
DF of the other model.
For an isotropic or constant-anisotropy component,
\(\beta_{\rm c}\) is free and the \(R_{\rm a}\) column stays
at the component’s own value, infinity, with a zero gradient,
because the isotropic and constant-anisotropy models have no
anisotropy radius. Default: `()`, which means no anisotropy
parameter is a parameter of the likelihood.

Returns:

**likelihood** – The log-likelihood as a JAX function of the component weights, the
mass and length scales and, for the components in free, the
anisotropy parameters. A call of the Likelihood without arguments
returns the value at the model’s own weights and scales, the value
log_likelihood returns.

Return type:

[Likelihood](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Likelihood)

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If model is not a Model, or model has several components and
    is not a superposition.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If data is empty or holds an object that is not a Data.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the data are in several unit systems, or in a unit system other
    than the unit system of model (Model.to presents a model in
    another unit system).

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If free repeats a component index or lists a component index that
    model does not have.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a free component is not spatially finite, is not a DF on a
    truncated profile that carries the DF of another model, or has an
    anisotropy model with neither a \(\beta_{\rm c}\) nor an
    \(R_{\rm a}\).

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If free is given together with binned distributions or
    Gauss-Hermite moments.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the projected tables of the components differ in the innermost
    tabulated radius, the outermost tabulated radius or the edge radius.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a projected radius of `"sigma_los"` data lies inside the
    innermost or beyond the outermost projected radius of the model’s
    table. The likelihood does not extrapolate the table.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If Gauss-Hermite moments at projected radii are given on a
    superposition, or a projected radius of the moments lies outside the
    projected radii of the model’s table of moments. A superposition
    takes Gauss-Hermite moments in apertures only.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If an aperture encloses no tabulated surface density, or if the disk
    inside the innermost tabulated projected radius carries more than
    \(10^{-6}\) of the aperture’s weight.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the 3D radius of `"pdf_v"` data lies outside the profile or,
    for a Type II model, at or beyond the anisotropy radius.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the error of a component’s accuracy check exceeds
    \(10^{-2}\) and the component’s settings do not set
    `write_anyway=True`.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the projection gives a negative squared line-of-sight dispersion.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If a table of velocity distributions fails the table’s own
    consistency check (for binned distributions and Gauss-Hermite
    moments).

- [**WorkerError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.WorkerError) – If a parallel process ends while a table of velocity distributions
    is computed (for binned distributions and Gauss-Hermite moments).

See also

[`log_likelihood`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.log_likelihood)
The log-likelihood at the model’s own weights and scales.

[`Likelihood`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Likelihood)
The JAX function likelihood returns.

[`Data`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Data)
The measurements a model is compared with.

`superpose`
A superposition of models that share one density.

Notes

Each dispersion measurement \(i\) is the mean of
\(\sigma_{\rm los}^2\) over the measurement’s nodes \(x_j\),
weighted by the node weights \(q_{ij}\) and the surface density
\(\Sigma\),

\[\sigma_i^2 = \frac{\sum_j q_{ij}\, \Sigma(x_j)\,
\sigma_{\rm los}^2(x_j)}{\sum_j q_{ij}\, \Sigma(x_j)}.\]

A projected radius has one node, the projected radius itself. An
aperture has the nodes and weights of sigma_los_aperture. On a
superposition, each component’s table is the component’s own table on
the shared density, and the component weights mix the numerator and
the denominator of \(\sigma_i^2\) (mixture), so each measurement
is a ratio of two sums linear in the weights. A length scale \(l\)
other than the model’s own length scale moves each node to
\(x_j = R_j / (L\,l)\) and keeps the node weights \(q_{ij}\):
the move is a change of variable to the projected radius of the data,
in which the aperture is fixed.

A free component’s tables at an anisotropy \(\theta\) are computed
at the first call of the Likelihood at \(\theta\): first the
component’s DF on the component’s truncated profile, then the
component’s two projected tables, with the tabulated radii placed for
\(\theta\). Where the DF cannot be built at \(\theta\), the
Likelihood returns minus infinity. The gradient in \(\theta\) is
the gradient of the reading at the placed radii, with the placed radii
held fixed. Between two placements of the radii, the value changes by
no more than the tolerance of the tables. An untruncated component
cannot be free, because the edge terms of an untruncated component read
the component’s DF.

A Gauss-Hermite moment (`"h3"` or `"h4"`) in an aperture is the
moment of the mixture’s velocity distribution in the aperture. The
mixture’s distribution is the sum of the components’ distributions
(aperture_losvd), each weighted by the component weight and the
component’s projected mass, and the moment is taken about the
mixture’s own mean velocity, in units of the mixture’s own dispersion.
A moment in an aperture is differentiable in the weights and does not
depend on the mass scale. The distributions in apertures are computed
at the model’s own radii, so the length scale stays at the model’s own
length scale. A Gauss-Hermite moment at a projected radius is read on a
model of one component from a table of the model’s moments over
projected radius, at the projected radius that the length scale moves,
so a moment at a projected radius is also differentiable in the length
scale. Neither kind of Gauss-Hermite moment is taken together with a
free component.

Each call of likelihood computes the projected table of every
component. For many evaluations on one model, call likelihood once
and call the returned Likelihood many times.

References

Notes Section T:7.4.

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> model = pp.solve(pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()))
>>> data = pp.Data(
...     "sigma_los", [0.30, 0.25], r_2d=[0.5, 1.0], errors=[0.01, 0.01]
... )
>>> like = pp.likelihood(model, data)
>>> like.weights.shape
(1,)
>>> bool(float(like()) > float("-inf"))
True
```

pianistpy.inference.log_likelihood(*model*, *data*, *settings=None*)

Return the Gaussian log-likelihood of a model against data.

log_likelihood returns one number, the value of likelihood at the
model’s own component weights and scales. For many evaluations, or for
gradients, call likelihood once and call the returned Likelihood.

Parameters:

- **model** ([*Model*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df#pianistpy.df.Model)) – A model of one component, or a superposition (superpose), in the
unit system of the data.

- **data** ([*Data*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Data)* or **sequence** of *[*Data*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Data)) – The measurements. The log-likelihoods of several Data are summed.

- **settings** ([*Settings*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings#pianistpy.settings.Settings)*, **optional*) – The numerical settings of the observables. Default: `None`, which
means the model’s own settings.

Returns:

**log_likelihood** – The Gaussian log-likelihood at the model’s own component weights
and scales, summed over the data. The value is minus infinity where
the nodes of a measurement carry no surface density or where a
projected radius of the data lies inside the innermost tabulated
projected radius.

Return type:

[float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If model and data cannot be compared, under each condition the
    Raises section of likelihood lists for InputError.

- [**AccuracyError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError) – If the error of a component’s accuracy check exceeds
    \(10^{-2}\) and the component’s settings do not set
    `write_anyway=True`, or if the projection gives a negative squared
    line-of-sight dispersion.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If a table of velocity distributions fails the table’s own
    consistency check (for binned distributions and Gauss-Hermite
    moments).

- [**WorkerError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.WorkerError) – If a parallel process ends while a table of velocity distributions
    is computed (for binned distributions and Gauss-Hermite moments).

See also

[`likelihood`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.likelihood)
The log-likelihood as a JAX function of the parameters.

[`Data`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/inference#pianistpy.inference.Data)
The measurements a model is compared with.

Notes

For residuals \(r\) of the measured values minus the model’s values
and the covariance matrix \(C\) of the errors (diagonal, with
\(C_{ii} = e_i^2\), for independent errors \(e_i\)),

\[\ln \mathcal{L} = -\frac{1}{2} r^{\rm T} C^{-1} r
- \frac{1}{2} \ln \det (2 \pi C).\]

References

Notes Section T:7.4.

Examples

```python
>>> import pianistpy as pp
>>> from pianistpy.inference import log_likelihood
>>> model = pp.solve(pp.Component(pp.DoublePowerLaw.hernquist()))
>>> data = pp.Data(
...     "sigma_los", [0.30, 0.25], r_2d=[0.5, 1.0], errors=[0.01, 0.01]
... )
>>> value = log_likelihood(model, data)
>>> isinstance(value, float)
True
```

# Units

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units

Module `pianistpy.units`

Unit systems of results and conversion factors out of internal units.

A result presents the result’s quantities in another unit system through the result’s
`to` method, which builds a Units object. unit_factors returns the
conversion factors of a density profile as a UnitFactors object.

class pianistpy.units.UnitFactors(*rho_norm*, *mass_q*, *model_v*, *model_mass*, *model_rho*, *model_p*, *physical_r_pc=None*, *physical_v_kms=None*, *physical_mass_msun=None*, *physical_rho_msun_pc3=None*, *physical_p_kms2=None*, *physical_rho_0_msun_pc3=None*)

Factors that convert quantities from internal units to model and physical units.

A quantity in internal units is multiplied by the factor of the
quantity’s dimension to obtain the quantity in the target units. The
model units have \(G = M_0 = r_0 = 1\), with \(M_0\) the mass
inside the radius \(c\,r_0\) and \(c\) the concentration given to
unit_factors. A length has no model factor, because internal units and
model units both measure a length in units of \(r_0\).

Parameters:

- **rho_norm** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Normalization \(C\) of the density profile
(DoublePowerLaw.rho_norm).

- **mass_q** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The number \(q = \mathcal{M}(c)/C\): the mass inside the radius
\(c\,r_0\) in units of \(4\pi\rho_0 r_0^3\).

- **model_v** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Factor that converts a velocity to model units, \((C q)^{-1/2}\).

- **model_mass** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Factor that converts a mass to model units, \((C q)^{-1}\).

- **model_rho** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Factor that converts a density to model units,
\((4\pi C q)^{-1}\).

- **model_p** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Factor that converts a potential to model units, \((C q)^{-1}\).

- **physical_r_pc** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **None**, **optional*) – Factor that converts a length to parsecs, equal to \(r_0\) in
parsecs. Default: `None`, which means unit_factors received no
physical scales.

- **physical_v_kms** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **None**, **optional*) – Factor that converts a velocity to kilometers per second. Default:
`None`, which means unit_factors received no physical scales.

- **physical_mass_msun** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **None**, **optional*) – Factor that converts a mass to solar masses. Default: `None`, which
means unit_factors received no physical scales.

- **physical_rho_msun_pc3** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **None**, **optional*) – Factor that converts a density to solar masses per cubic parsec.
Default: `None`, which means unit_factors received no physical
scales.

- **physical_p_kms2** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **None**, **optional*) – Factor that converts a potential to the square of kilometers per
second. Default: `None`, which means unit_factors received no
physical scales.

- **physical_rho_0_msun_pc3** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **None**, **optional*) – The scale density \(\rho_0\) in solar masses per cubic parsec.
Default: `None`, which means unit_factors received no physical
scales.

See also

[`unit_factors`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.unit_factors)
The function that builds the factors of a density profile.

[`Units`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units)
The unit system a result carries.

Notes

Every physical factor is None unless unit_factors received both
physical scales, \(M_0\) in solar masses and \(r_0\) in parsecs.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy import DoublePowerLaw
>>> from pianistpy.units import unit_factors
>>> factors = unit_factors(DoublePowerLaw.nfw(), concentration=10.0)
>>> round(factors.model_mass, 6)
0.67168
>>> factors.physical_r_pc is None
True
```

class pianistpy.units.Units(*system='internal'*, *concentration=None*, *mass_0_msun=None*, *r_0_pc=None*)

The unit system of a result and the scales that define the unit system.

A result holds the result’s numbers in internal units and hands the
numbers over in the unit system that the result’s Units object sets.
Units.build builds a Units object from scales in any unit; the
constructor takes the scales in solar masses and parsecs.

Parameters:

- **system** (*{"internal"**, **"model"**, **"physical"}**, **optional*) – The unit system. `"internal"`: \(G = \rho_0/C = r_0 = 1\), with
\(\rho_0\) the scale density and \(C\) the normalization of
the density profile. `"model"`: \(G = M_0 = r_0 = 1\), with
\(M_0\) the mass inside the radius \(c\,r_0\).
`"physical"`: Astropy quantities in parsecs, kilometers per second,
solar masses, solar masses per cubic parsec and
\({\rm km^2\,s^{-2}}\). Default: `"internal"`, which means the
result hands the result’s quantities over in internal units.

- **concentration** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – The concentration \(c\), which defines \(M_0\) as the mass
inside the radius \(c\,r_0\). Required by the model units and the
physical units. Default: `None`, which means no concentration, as
the internal units require.

- **mass_0_msun** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – The mass \(M_0\) in solar masses. Required by the physical units.
Default: `None`, which means no physical mass scale.

- **r_0_pc** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – The scale radius \(r_0\) in parsecs. Required by the physical
units. Default: `None`, which means no physical length scale.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If system is not `"internal"`, `"model"` or `"physical"`.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If system is `"model"` or `"physical"` and concentration is
    None.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If system is `"physical"` and mass_0_msun or r_0_pc is None.

See also

[`Units.build`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units.build)
The units of a unit system from scales in any unit.

[`unit_factors`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.unit_factors)
The conversion factors out of internal units.

[`UnitFactors`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.UnitFactors)
The conversion factors and their definitions.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy.units import Units
>>> Units().system
'internal'
>>> Units.build("model", concentration=10.0).concentration
10.0
>>> units = Units.build("physical", concentration=10.0, mass_0=1e12, r_vir=2e5)
>>> units.r_0_pc
20000.0
```

classmethod build(*system*, *concentration=None*, *mass_0=None*, *r_0=None*, *r_vir=None*)

Return the units of a unit system from user-specified scales in any unit.

The internal units ignore every scale. The model units keep the
concentration and ignore the physical scales. The physical units keep
the concentration, \(M_0\) in solar masses and \(r_0\) in
parsecs.

Parameters:

- **system** (*{"internal"**, **"model"**, **"physical"}*) – The unit system of the returned units.

- **concentration** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – The concentration \(c\), which defines \(M_0\) as the mass
inside the radius \(c\,r_0\). Positive. Required by the model
units and the physical units. Default: `None`, which means no
concentration.

- **mass_0** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **astropy Quantity**, **optional*) – The mass \(M_0\). A float is in solar masses; a quantity of any
mass unit is converted to solar masses. Positive. Required by the
physical units. Default: `None`, which means no mass scale.

- **r_0** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **astropy Quantity**, **optional*) – The scale radius \(r_0\). A float is in parsecs; a quantity of
any length unit is converted to parsecs. Positive. Default:
`None`, which means the scale radius is taken from r_vir.

- **r_vir** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or **astropy Quantity**, **optional*) – The radius \(c\,r_0\), given in place of r_0. A float is in
parsecs; a quantity of any length unit is converted to parsecs.
Positive. Default: `None`, which means the scale radius is
taken from r_0.

Returns:

**units** – The units of system, with \(M_0\) in solar masses and
\(r_0\) in parsecs.

Return type:

[Units](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units)

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If both r_0 and r_vir are given.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If concentration, r_0, r_vir or, for the physical units,
    mass_0 is given and is not positive.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If r_vir is given and concentration is not.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If system is not `"internal"`, `"model"` or `"physical"`.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If system is `"model"` or `"physical"` and concentration
    is None.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If system is `"physical"` and mass_0 is None, or neither
    r_0 nor r_vir is given.

See also

`Model.to`
The model presented in the unit system that a Units object sets.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy.units import Units
>>> Units.build("internal", concentration=10.0)
Units(system='internal', concentration=None, mass_0_msun=None, r_0_pc=None)
>>> Units.build("physical", concentration=10.0, mass_0=1e12, r_0=2e4).r_0_pc
20000.0
```

factors(*profile*)

Return the conversion factors of the units’ scales for a density profile.

Parameters:

**profile** ([*DoublePowerLaw*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/profiles#pianistpy.profiles.DoublePowerLaw)) – The density profile, which fixes the normalization \(C\) of
the density.

Returns:

**factors** – The factors unit_factors returns for the profile, the units’
concentration, and the units’ mass_0_msun and r_0_pc.

Return type:

[UnitFactors](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.UnitFactors)

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the units’ concentration is None, as in the internal units.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the units’ concentration is not positive.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If one of mass_0_msun and r_0_pc is set and the other is None.

See also

[`unit_factors`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.unit_factors)
The function that builds the factors.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy import DoublePowerLaw
>>> from pianistpy.units import Units
>>> units = Units.build("model", concentration=10.0)
>>> round(units.factors(DoublePowerLaw.nfw()).model_mass, 6)
0.67168
```

convert(*kind*, *value*, *profile*)

Return a quantity given in internal units in the unit system of the units.

Parameters:

- **kind** (*{"length"**, **"velocity"**, **"mass"**, **"density"**, **"potential"}*) – The physical dimension of the quantity.

- **value** (*array-like*) – The quantity, in internal units.

- **profile** ([*DoublePowerLaw*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/profiles#pianistpy.profiles.DoublePowerLaw)) – The density profile, which fixes the normalization \(C\) of
the density.

Returns:

**converted** – The quantity, with the shape of value. A float64 array in the
internal units and in the model units; an Astropy quantity in the
physical units. A length has the same value in internal units and
in model units, because both unit systems measure a length in
units of \(r_0\).

Return type:

array or astropy Quantity

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If kind is not `"length"`, `"velocity"`, `"mass"`,
    `"density"` or `"potential"`.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the unit system is not the internal one and factors raises
    InputError for the units’ scales.

See also

[`Units.factors`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units.factors)
The conversion factors the conversion multiplies by.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy import DoublePowerLaw
>>> from pianistpy.units import Units
>>> units = Units.build("model", concentration=10.0)
>>> units.convert("length", [1.0, 2.0], DoublePowerLaw.nfw())
array([1., 2.])
>>> round(float(units.convert("mass", 1.0, DoublePowerLaw.nfw())), 6)
0.67168
```

to_dict()

Return the units as a dictionary of plain values.

Returns:

**record** – The keys `system`, `concentration`, `mass_0_msun` and
`r_0_pc`, with the values of the units’ fields, in the form
from_dict reads.

Return type:

[dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

See also

[`Units.from_dict`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units.from_dict)
The units rebuilt from the dictionary.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy.units import Units
>>> record = Units.build("model", concentration=10.0).to_dict()
>>> record["system"], record["concentration"], record["r_0_pc"]
('model', 10.0, None)
```

classmethod from_dict(*record*)

Return the units that a dictionary written by to_dict records.

Parameters:

**record** (*mapping** or **None*) – The dictionary to_dict writes. None or an empty mapping stands
for the internal units.

Returns:

**units** – The units the dictionary records.

Return type:

[Units](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units)

Raises:

[**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If the recorded unit system and scales raise InputError in the
    Units constructor.

See also

[`Units.to_dict`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units.to_dict)
The dictionary of the units.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy.units import Units
>>> units = Units.build("model", concentration=10.0)
>>> Units.from_dict(units.to_dict()) == units
True
>>> Units.from_dict(None).system
'internal'
```

pianistpy.units.unit_factors(*profile*, *concentration*, *mass_0_msun=None*, *r_0_pc=None*)

Return the factors that convert a profile’s quantities out of internal units.

The model-unit factors depend on the density profile and the
concentration \(c\) alone. The physical factors also need the two
physical scales, \(M_0\) in solar masses and \(r_0\) in parsecs.

Parameters:

- **profile** ([*DoublePowerLaw*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/profiles#pianistpy.profiles.DoublePowerLaw)) – The density profile. The profile fixes the normalization \(C\)
and the mass \(\mathcal{M}(c)\) inside the radius \(c\,r_0\).

- **concentration** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The concentration \(c\): the radius, in units of the scale radius
\(r_0\), inside which the mass \(M_0\) is defined. Positive.

- **mass_0_msun** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – The mass \(M_0\) in solar masses. Positive. Given together with
r_0_pc or not at all. Default: `None`, which means only the
model-unit factors are formed.

- **r_0_pc** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*, **optional*) – The scale radius \(r_0\) in parsecs. Positive. Given together with
mass_0_msun or not at all. Default: `None`, which means only the
model-unit factors are formed.

Returns:

**factors** – The model-unit factors, and the physical factors when both
mass_0_msun and r_0_pc are given. Every physical factor is None
when neither mass_0_msun nor r_0_pc is given.

Return type:

[UnitFactors](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.UnitFactors)

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If concentration is not positive.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If one of mass_0_msun and r_0_pc is given and the other is not.

See also

[`UnitFactors`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.UnitFactors)
The factors and their definitions.

[`Units.factors`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units#pianistpy.units.Units.factors)
The factors for the scales a result carries.

Notes

With \(\rho_{\rm w} = \rho_0/C\), the internal unit of mass is
\(M_{\rm W} = 4\pi\rho_{\rm w} r_0^3\), the internal unit of velocity is
\(v_{\rm W} = (4\pi G\rho_{\rm w} r_0^2)^{1/2}\), and the mass inside
the radius \(c\,r_0\) is \(M_0 = 4\pi\rho_0 r_0^3\,q\). A velocity in
internal units is therefore multiplied by \((C q)^{-1/2}\) to reach
model units, a mass and a potential by \((C q)^{-1}\), and a density
by \((4\pi C q)^{-1}\).

References

[Chiang+(2026d)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28758), Section 2.1 and Eq. (6).

Examples

```python
>>> import math
>>> from pianistpy import DoublePowerLaw
>>> factors = unit_factors(DoublePowerLaw.nfw(), concentration=10.0)
>>> factors.rho_norm
1.0
>>> round(factors.mass_q, 12) == round(math.log(11.0) - 10.0 / 11.0, 12)
True
>>> physical = unit_factors(
...     DoublePowerLaw.nfw(), 10.0, mass_0_msun=1e12, r_0_pc=2e4
... )
>>> physical.physical_r_pc
20000.0
```


---

# Results and files

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io

Module `pianistpy.io`

Writing results to files and reading results back from files.

A result is written by the result’s `write` method and read back by read.
write_result and read_result implement the HDF5 file format that the
`write` methods and read share. write_table exports columns of a result,
each with a column name, as a text table.

class pianistpy.io.StoredResult(*kind*, *identity*, *data_sha256*, *record*, *arrays*, *parents*, *provenance*)

A result as one file stores the result.

read_result returns a StoredResult; the reader registered for the
result’s kind (register_reader) rebuilds the result object from the
StoredResult.

Parameters:

- **kind** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The kind of result, for example `"model"`.

- **identity** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The identity string of the result.

- **data_sha256** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The SHA-256 digest of the file’s datasets (data_digest), as a
hexadecimal string of 64 characters.

- **record** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – The inputs and settings that determine the result, in dictionary form.

- **arrays** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)* of **str to array*) – The arrays of the result, by name.

- **parents** ([*tuple*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)* of *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The identity strings of the results from which the result was
computed.

- **provenance** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)* of **str to str*) – The creation date of the file and the versions and numerical backend
of the session that wrote the file (backend_provenance).

See also

[`read_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.read_result)
The function that reads a file into a StoredResult.

[`write_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.write_result)
The function that writes a result to a file.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import read_result, write_result
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "example.h5")
...     arrays = {"x": np.arange(3.0)}
...     _ = write_result(path, "example", "example-1", {"n": 3}, arrays)
...     stored = read_result(path)
>>> stored.kind, stored.identity, stored.record, stored.parents
('example', 'example-1', {'n': 3}, ())
>>> stored.arrays["x"]
array([0., 1., 2.])
```

pianistpy.io.backend_provenance()

Return the software versions and the numerical backend of the running session.

write_result stores the returned dictionary in every file the function
writes.

Returns:

**provenance** – The keys `python_version`, `numpy_version` and `scipy_version`;
`jax_platforms_env` and `pianistpy_platform_env`, the values of
the environment variables `JAX_PLATFORMS` and
`PIANISTPY_PLATFORM`, each `"unset"` where the variable is not
set; and `jax_version`, `jax_backend` and `jax_devices`. A
session in which JAX cannot be imported records `"unavailable"` for
`jax_version` and `jax_devices` and `"none"` for
`jax_backend`.

Return type:

[dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) of str to str

See also

[`write_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.write_result)
The function that stores the provenance in each file.

Examples

```python
>>> from pianistpy.io import backend_provenance
>>> sorted(backend_provenance())[:3]
['jax_backend', 'jax_devices', 'jax_platforms_env']
```

pianistpy.io.data_digest(*source*)

Return the SHA-256 digest of every dataset of an HDF5 file or group.

The digest covers every dataset, in the sorted order of the datasets’
paths: each dataset’s path, data type, shape and raw bytes. The digest
excludes the attributes, so a file can store the digest of its own
datasets as an attribute.

Parameters:

**source** (*h5py.Group** or **path*) – An open HDF5 file or group, or the path of an HDF5 file.

Returns:

**digest** – The hexadecimal digest, 64 characters.

Return type:

[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

See also

[`write_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.write_result)
The function that records the digest in each file the function writes.

[`read_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.read_result)
The function that compares the recorded digest with a recomputed digest.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import data_digest, write_result
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "example.h5")
...     written = write_result(path, "example", "example-1", {}, {"x": np.ones(2)})
...     recomputed = data_digest(path)
>>> recomputed == written, len(recomputed)
(True, 64)
```

pianistpy.io.load_result(*source*)

Return a StoredResult, given the StoredResult or the path of a result file.

A StoredResult passed as source is returned unchanged. A path is read
and checked by read_result.

Parameters:

**source** ([*StoredResult*](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.StoredResult)* or *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* or **path-like*) – A StoredResult, or the path of a file that holds one result.

Returns:

**stored** – source itself when source is a StoredResult; otherwise the
StoredResult that read_result reads from the file.

Return type:

[StoredResult](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.StoredResult)

Raises:

[**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If source is a path and read_result raises ResultError: the file
    lacks an attribute of a result file, the major number of the file’s
    format version differs from the major number the package reads, or
    the recomputed digest differs from the recorded digest.

See also

[`read_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.read_result)
The function that reads and checks a file.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import load_result, read_result, write_result
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "example.h5")
...     _ = write_result(path, "example", "example-1", {}, {"x": np.ones(2)})
...     stored = load_result(path)
>>> load_result(stored) is stored
True
```

pianistpy.io.read(*path*)

Read a result from a file, whatever kind of result the file holds.

The call reads and checks the file with read_result and passes the
StoredResult to the reader registered for the file’s kind
(register_reader).

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* or **path-like*) – A file written by the `write` method of a result.

Returns:

**result** – The distribution function, model, particles or other result the file
holds, equal to the result that was written.

Return type:

[object](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Raises:

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the file lacks one of the attributes `format_version`,
    `result_kind`, `identity`, `data_sha256`, `record` and
    `parents`.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the major number of the file’s format version differs from the
    major number of the format version the installed package reads.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the recomputed digest of the datasets differs from the digest the
    file records.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If no reader is registered for the kind the file records.

See also

[`register_reader`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.register_reader)
The registration of the function that rebuilds a kind.

[`read_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.read_result)
The read and the check of the file.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import read, register_reader, write_result
>>> register_reader("doc_example", lambda stored: float(stored.arrays["x"].sum()))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "example.h5")
...     arrays = {"x": np.arange(3.0)}
...     _ = write_result(path, "doc_example", "example-1", {}, arrays)
...     result = read(path)
>>> result
3.0
```

pianistpy.io.read_result(*path*)

Read one result from an HDF5 file and check the file’s digest.

The call recomputes the SHA-256 digest of the file’s datasets
(data_digest) and compares the recomputed digest with the digest the
file records.

Parameters:

**path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* or **path-like*) – The file to read.

Returns:

**stored** – The arrays, record, identity string, digest, parents and provenance
the file holds.

Return type:

[StoredResult](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.StoredResult)

Raises:

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the file lacks one of the attributes `format_version`,
    `result_kind`, `identity`, `data_sha256`, `record` and
    `parents`.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the major number of the file’s format version differs from the
    major number of the format version the installed package reads.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the recomputed digest differs from the digest the file records.

See also

[`read`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.read)
The function that rebuilds the result object from the file.

[`write_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.write_result)
The function that writes the file.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import read_result, write_result
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "example.h5")
...     arrays = {"x": np.arange(3.0)}
...     _ = write_result(path, "example", "example-1", {"n": 3}, arrays)
...     stored = read_result(path)
>>> stored.record, stored.arrays["x"]
({'n': 3}, array([0., 1., 2.]))
```

pianistpy.io.register_reader(*kind*, *reader*)

Make reader the function that rebuilds every result of one kind.

read calls the function registered for the kind a file records. A
second registration for the same kind replaces the first registration.

Parameters:

- **kind** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The kind of result, as write_result stores the kind in the file.

- **reader** (*callable*) – A function that takes the StoredResult and returns the result
object.

Return type:

None

See also

[`read`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.read)
The function that calls the registered reader.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import read, register_reader, write_result
>>> register_reader("doc_example", lambda stored: float(stored.arrays["x"].sum()))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "example.h5")
...     arrays = {"x": np.arange(3.0)}
...     _ = write_result(path, "doc_example", "example-1", {}, arrays)
...     total = read(path)
>>> total
3.0
```

pianistpy.io.write_result(*path*, *kind*, *identity*, *record*, *arrays*, *parents=()*, *overwrite=False*)

Write one result to an HDF5 file and check the file against the request.

After writing, the call reads the file back and compares the file’s
arrays, bit for bit, and the file’s record, identity string, kind and
parents with the values passed. The call stores the SHA-256 digest of the
datasets (data_digest) in the file only when every comparison holds.

Parameters:

- **path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* or **path-like*) – The file to write.

- **kind** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The kind of result, the key under which register_reader finds the
function that rebuilds the result.

- **identity** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The identity string of the result.

- **record** (*mapping*) – The inputs and settings that determine the result, in dictionary
form. Every value is one that `json.dumps` writes.

- **arrays** (*mapping** of **str to array-like*) – The arrays of the result, by name. A name may contain `/` to place
the array in an HDF5 group.

- **parents** (*sequence** of *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*, **optional*) – The identity strings of the results from which the result was
computed. Default: `()`, which means the result has no parent
results.

- **overwrite** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*, **optional*) – Whether to replace an existing file at path. Default: `False`,
which means an existing file is kept and the call raises
InputError.

Returns:

**data_sha256** – The SHA-256 digest of the datasets as written (data_digest), the
same digest the file stores.

Return type:

[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a file exists at path and overwrite is false.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If the file read back differs from the request in an array, the
    record, the identity string, the kind or the parents.

See also

[`read_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.read_result)
The function that reads the file back.

[`data_digest`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.data_digest)
The digest of the datasets.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import write_result
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "example.h5")
...     digest = write_result(path, "example", "example-1", {}, {"x": np.ones(2)})
>>> len(digest)
64
```

pianistpy.io.write_table(*path*, *columns*, *header=()*, *overwrite=False*)

Write columns, each with a column name, as a fixed-width text table.

The file opens with the lines of header, each prefixed with `# ``,
followed by the line ``# columns:` and the column names in order. Each
following row holds one value of every column, each value in a field of
25 characters: a float in exponent form with 14 digits after the decimal
point, an integer as the integer. After writing, the call reads the file
back with `numpy.loadtxt` and compares the values read with the values
written, rounded to the 14 digits the file holds.

Parameters:

- **path** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* or **path-like*) – The file to write.

- **columns** (*mapping** of **str to array-like*) – The columns, in order. Each column is one-dimensional, of integer or
float type, and of the length of every other column. Each column name
is non-empty and holds no whitespace.

- **header** (*sequence** of *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*, **optional*) – The lines at the head of the file, each without the leading `#`.
Default: `()`, which means the head holds only the line of column
names.

- **overwrite** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*, **optional*) – Whether to replace an existing file at path. Default: `False`,
which means an existing file is kept and the call raises
InputError.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a file exists at path and overwrite is false.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If columns is empty.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a column name is empty or holds whitespace.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a column is not one-dimensional.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a column is not of integer or float type.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If two columns differ in length.

- [**ResultError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError) – If a value read back differs from the value written, rounded to 14
    digits after the decimal point.

Return type:

None

See also

[`write_result`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/io#pianistpy.io.write_result)
The HDF5 file that records a result.

Examples

```python
>>> import os
>>> import tempfile
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from pianistpy.io import write_table
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
...     path = os.path.join(folder, "table.txt")
...     columns = {"r": np.array([1.0, 2.0]), "n": np.array([3, 4])}
...     write_table(path, columns, header=["radii and counts"])
...     with open(path) as file:
...         print(file.read(), end="")
# radii and counts
# columns: r n
1.00000000000000e+00     3
2.00000000000000e+00     4
```


---

# Settings

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings

Module `pianistpy.settings`

The numerical settings of a computation: the default settings, the quick
settings, and single fields changed by an expert.

A user passes a Settings object to a computation, for example
`pp.solve(component, settings=pp.Settings(quick=True))`. The default
settings and the quick settings are the two tested settings levels: the
package states the accuracy of each level from its test suite. The quick
settings use fewer nodes and rows than the default settings and hold every
check of a result to the same bounds, \(10^{-6}\), \(10^{-4}\) and
\(10^{-2}\). The manual’s settings tables list every field with its
value at each level.

class pianistpy.settings.Field(*default*, *doc*, *quick=None*)

One numerical setting: its value at each settings level and a
description of what the setting controls.

Parameters:

- **default** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*, *[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *[*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The field’s value in the default settings. The type of default is
the type every value of the field must have.

- **doc** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A description of what the field controls, as the manual’s settings
tables print it.

- **quick** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*, *[*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*, *[*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* or *[*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*, **optional*) – The field’s value in the quick settings. Default: `None`, which
means the quick settings use the value default.

See also

[`Settings`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings#pianistpy.settings.Settings)
The settings of a computation.

`FIELDS`
Every field of every group.

Examples

```python
>>> field = FIELDS["sampling"]["n_nodes"]
>>> field.value("default"), field.value("quick")
(2048, 512)
```

value(*level*)

Return the field’s value at a settings level.

Parameters:

**level** (*{"default"**, **"quick"}*) – The settings level.

Returns:

**value** – The field’s value in the quick settings if level is
`"quick"` and the field has a quick value; the field’s value
in the default settings otherwise.

Return type:

[bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) or [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

class pianistpy.settings.Settings(*quick=False*, *write_anyway=False*, *check_rows=False*, ***overrides*)

The numerical settings of a computation.

A Settings object starts from one of the two tested settings levels,
the default settings or the quick settings, and may change single
fields of a group. A result records its settings; a result made with a
changed field records that its settings are not a tested settings level
and lists each changed field.

Parameters:

- **quick** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*, **optional*) – Whether the settings start from the quick settings. Default:
`False`, which means the settings start from the default settings.

- **write_anyway** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*, **optional*) – Whether a computation returns a result whose own check is above
\(10^{-2}\) instead of raising AccuracyError. The returned
result’s validation report has the band `"refused"`, and an
AccuracyWarning is issued in place of the error. A model that
is not a physical equilibrium raises UnphysicalModelError
whatever the value of write_anyway. Default: `False`, which
means a result above \(10^{-2}\) raises AccuracyError.

- **check_rows** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*, **optional*) – Whether a gradient through a LosTable recomputes each
line-of-sight velocity distribution the gradient reads and compares
the recomputed distribution with the stored distribution. A
recomputed distribution must equal the stored distribution bit for
bit, and a JAX copy of the distribution’s computation (the twin
that carries the derivative) must agree with the stored
distribution to \(10^{-12}\) of the distribution’s largest
value; otherwise the gradient raises ResultError. The gradient’s value is
the same with and without the comparison; the comparison computes
each distribution read a second time. Default: `False`, which
means no distribution is recomputed.

- ****overrides** (*mapping*) – For each group to change (`inversion`, `truncation`,
`sampling`, `observables` or `losvd`), a mapping from field
name to new value. The manual’s settings tables list every field.
Default: no override, which means every field has its value at the
settings level.

Variables:

- **level** (*{"default"**, **"quick"}*) – The settings level the settings start from.

- **write_anyway** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether a result above \(10^{-2}\) is returned instead of
raising AccuracyError.

- **check_rows** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether a gradient through a LosTable recomputes and compares
each distribution the gradient reads.

- **overrides** (*mapping*) – For each changed group, the changed fields and their values. Read
only.

- **is_tested_level** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether no field is changed from the settings level.

Raises:

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If write_anyway or check_rows is not a bool.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a keyword of overrides is not a group name.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a field of an override is not a field of the override’s group.

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If an override’s value does not have the type of the field’s
    default value (an int is accepted for a float field).

- [**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If a number override is zero or negative, except a field whose name
    starts with `log10_` and the value 0 of `innermost_read_radius`
    and `outer_mass_share`.

See also

`FIELDS`
Every field of every group with its value at each level.

`LEVELS`
The names of the two tested settings levels.

Examples

```python
>>> Settings().level
'default'
>>> Settings(quick=True).is_tested_level
True
>>> Settings(inversion={"n_nodes": 256}).is_tested_level
False
>>> Settings(inversion={"n_nodes": 256}).inversion["n_nodes"]
256
>>> Settings().truncation["ode_rtol"]
1e-11
```

property level: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

The settings level the settings start from, `"default"` or
`"quick"`.

property write_anyway: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether a result above \(10^{-2}\) is returned instead of
raising AccuracyError.

property check_rows: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether a gradient through a LosTable recomputes and compares
each distribution the gradient reads.

property overrides: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

For each changed group, the changed fields and their values.

property is_tested_level: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

Whether no field is changed from the settings level.

group(*name*)

Return the value in force of every field of one group.

Parameters:

**name** (*{"inversion"**, **"truncation"**, **"sampling"**, **"observables"**, **"losvd"}*) – The group’s name.

Returns:

**values** – Each field of the group mapped to the field’s override if the
settings change the field, and to the field’s value at the
settings level otherwise. Read only.

Return type:

mapping

Raises:

[**InputError**](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/exceptions#pianistpy.exceptions.InputError) – If name is not a group name.

See also

[`resolved`](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/settings#pianistpy.settings.Settings.resolved)
The values in force of every group.

Examples

```python
>>> Settings(quick=True).group("sampling")["n_nodes"]
512
```

property inversion: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

The values in force of the group `inversion`.

property truncation: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

The values in force of the group `truncation`.

property sampling: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

The values in force of the group `sampling`.

property observables: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

The values in force of the group `observables`.

property losvd: [Mapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

The values in force of the group `losvd`.

resolved()

Return the value in force of every field of every group.

Returns:

their values in force.

Return type:

[dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```

to_dict()

Return the settings as the dictionary written to result files.

Returns:

and `"write_anyway": True` and `"check_rows": True` if the
settings set those options.

```

numerical()

Return the settings that determine a result’s values: the
settings level and the overrides.

A result’s identity is computed from this dictionary, so that two
results computed with the same level and overrides share an
identity whatever their write_anyway and check_rows.

Returns:

mapped to its changed fields and their values).

```

classmethod from_dict(*record*)

Build settings from the dictionary that to_dict writes.

entry’s former name, and else as `"default"`.

Returns:

Examples

>>> Settings.from_dict(settings.to_dict()) == settings

```
